extracted.intended_audience: Scientists applying for HFSP Research Grants (teams of independent researchers; Principal Applicants and Co-Applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing and submitting Letters of Intent and Full Proposals to the Human Frontier Science Program (HFSP) Research Grants (Program and Early Career) for award year 2027, including eligibility, scope, budget, ethics, and review criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core evaluation values
rubrics_metrics.description: HFSPO attaches highest importance to novelty, scientific merit, internationality, and interdisciplinarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These four elements are overarching priorities for HFSP-supported projects and should be evident in the application. Novelty implies challenging existing paradigms; scientific merit implies addressing important fundamental problems; internationality implies cross-national collaborations (preferably intercontinental); interdisciplinarity implies inclusion of expertise from outside traditional life sciences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty / frontier potential
rubrics_metrics.description: HFSP supports projects that challenge existing paradigms and extend the frontiers of life sciences by using novel approaches and techniques. The potential of a project to extend the frontiers of life sciences and lead to a breakthrough is a major criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary results are not required to stimulate daring ideas and high-risk development. Projects that are obvious next steps, use standard approaches, or promise only incremental advancement are not funded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific merit / transformative potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects should be potentially transformative in addressing important fundamental problems at the frontiers of the life sciences or in crossing barriers to progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate how the research could lead to breakthroughs; reviewers will assess the project's potential to extend the present frontier rather than incremental contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internationality of the team
rubrics_metrics.description: HFSP supports novel international, preferably intercontinental, collaborations that involve scientific exchanges across national boundaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teams should ideally include only one member per country; priority given to intercontinental collaborations. Inclusion of members from less represented countries is strongly encouraged. Teams with all members in one country are not eligible except in rare essential cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdisciplinarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Participation of scientists from disciplines outside the traditional life sciences (e.g., physics, chemistry, computational biology, engineering, mathematics, nanoscience, psychology) is highly encouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novel combinations of expertise are a major feature; truly novel interdisciplinary collaborations will have a higher chance of being awarded. RG-Early Career places special emphasis on interdisciplinarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team size and composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Teams must consist of normally 2-4 scientists (in specific cases 5). One member is designated Principal Applicant; others are Co-Applicants. All team members must hold a research doctoral degree and lead a research group; post-doctoral fellows are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Team members must be able to independently determine the course of the funded project and have freedom to administer the awarded grant. For award calculation, two members in the same country may be counted as 1.5 team members in rare cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: No prior collaboration / new collaborations
rubrics_metrics.description: Team members should not have collaborated before, will normally not have published original research together, and the project must be significantly different from their ongoing research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Co-authorship is generally considered evidence of past collaboration. Applicants must list co-publications between team members; more than three co-publications are very likely seen as proof of ongoing collaboration and strongly reduce the chance of funding. Some older or field-review joint publications may be acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinct research direction requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects must be distinctly different from all team members’ other research and propose new lines of research through the collaboration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals representing an obvious next step in the laboratory of one or more applicants or that do not represent significant changes in research direction are unlikely to receive funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Close collaboration necessity
rubrics_metrics.description: Close collaboration between all team members must be absolutely necessary to achieve the aims of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ‘Concerted action’ programs where each member performs a self-contained project under a general theme without extensive interaction are not considered collaborative and will not be supported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical and computational modelling expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematical or computational modelling approaches are strongly encouraged, but must be clearly described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include sufficient detail about mathematical methods and demonstrate appreciation of the limits of the proposed approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific scope — basic research only
rubrics_metrics.description: HFSP supports basic research studying fundamental problems in the life sciences across all levels (molecules to ecosystems).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funded projects should address a fundamental problem or mechanism at the frontier. Examples of funded topics are available on HFSP website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions — not funded topics
rubrics_metrics.description: HFSP does not fund projects of a purely applied nature (clinical/pharmaceutical focus, drug design), applied engineering/biotech/nanotechnology, development of novel methods not aiming to answer a basic biological question, projects directly focused on solving agricultural/forestry/environmental/conservation problems, purely observational/descriptive projects (including large-scale systematic screens or data-collection studies), or proposals that are obvious next steps or incremental.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the project falls into these excluded categories it will not be supported; applicants should ensure alignment with HFSP basic-research remit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary data and risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary data are not required; grant applications may be exploratory or discovery-oriented and may entail high risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are expected to address potential risks and outline mitigation strategies in the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Applicant institutional and geographic requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal Applicant must be working at a non-for-profit academic institution in an HFSPO member country (list provided). Former Career Development Awardees are an exception if team includes at least one Co-Applicant from an HFSP member country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principal Applicant is responsible for planning, coordinating the research, liaison with HFSPO, submitting annual distribution of funds and progress reports; must confirm institutional changes do not harm the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliation and secondary affiliation disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must declare all research-related affiliations, including secondary affiliations in different countries; affiliations listed on recent publications are generally considered research-related.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-member teams are not eligible if one has a secondary affiliation in the country of the other. Exceptions may be made case-by-case for field work or equipment use. Different branches/campuses of same university or organizations count as same affiliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teams including for-profit members
rubrics_metrics.description: Teams may include members from for-profit organizations if necessary, but such members may not receive any funds and will not be considered in calculating award amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In a two-member team with one member in a for-profit institution, the total annual award will be reduced to 150,000 USD. In other cases, for-profit members are excluded from award-size calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Grants – Program (RG-Program) priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: RG-Program are for teams of independent researchers at any career stage to develop new lines of research via new collaborations; priority to novel projects with potential to extend frontiers and teams including members from outside life sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are encouraged to include independent investigators early in careers and ensure high diversity of backgrounds and approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Grants – Early Career (RG-Early Career) eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: RG-Early Career awards encourage outstanding scientists in initial period of independent careers to propose novel research projects; Early Career members have completed one or two postdocs and been recently appointed to independent staff positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All members must be within 5 years of obtaining an independent position and have received their first doctoral degree no longer than 10 years prior to LOI deadline (extensions possible for parental leave/military/medical). Early Career applicants must be project leaders directing a research group with full responsibility and control of HFSP funds; postdocs are ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent application restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: No individual may be an applicant on more than one Letter of Intent in the same review cycle; scientists cannot hold or apply for more than one HFSP award at the same time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a team member appears on two or more LOIs, these will all be removed from competition. Applies across roles and HFSP award types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions for previous/present awardees
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientists cannot hold more than one HFSP award at any one time. Awardees from 2021 and 2022 may apply for a new grant if it starts after closure of current award and if project/team differ; awardees from 2023 and 2024 are not eligible to apply as Principal Applicant or Co-Applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications bearing strong similarity to previous awards in team composition or topic will not be eligible; awardees from 2021/2022 must provide previous grant details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letter of Intent pre-screening / eligibility check
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters of Intent will be checked for eligibility and pre-screened by a small committee for concordance with scientific scope and project requirements; projects not meeting requirements will not be sent for further review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure LOI clearly demonstrates adherence to sections 2 and 3 requirements. Initiation (saving the form) creates an LOI ID and must be done by initiation deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: LOI and application timeline requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Initiation of LOI (creating & saving online form) and submission deadlines are mandatory (dates given); Full Proposals are by invitation only after LOI review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initiation must create a 7-digit LOI ID by 17 March 2026; LOI submission by 26 March 2026; invited Full Proposals mid-September 2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award tenure and fixed award amounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Each grant is awarded for three years (funds can be used during a fourth year). Annual team sums: 2-member teams 300,000 USD; 3-member teams 400,000 USD; 4-member (or more) 500,000 USD (annual).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two members from same country counted as 1.5 members for award calculation (350k for 2.5, 450k for 3.5). Currency conversion applied at time of transfer; HFSPO reserves right to transfer local currency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds may be used for equipment essential for the new collaborative project; materials and supplies; services specific to the project; salaries for research assistants (postdocs, graduate students, technicians); communication expenses; travel and per diem (up to three months per year); costs for meetings/training and the annual awardee meeting; overheads up to 10% of direct costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equipment purchase must be essential for the new collaborative project. Consulting/computer/research-facility services specific to the project allowed. Indirect costs at each research institution limited to no more than 10% of direct costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impermissible expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: No salary support for the Principal Applicant, Co-Applicant or other faculty, institutional staff (secretaries, lab managers) and no student tuition fees may be paid from the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Salaries may be provided only for research assistants essential for the new collaborative project. Funds are not to replace basic institutional infrastructure or supplement domestic programmes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution and carryover of funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution of funds will be proposed by the team; after approval funds transferred directly to each team member’s institution. Funds remaining from an annual period may be carried over to the next one without prior approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HFSPO expects a fair distribution and a valid explanation for deviations from even distribution. Institutions must maintain lists of expenditures and supporting documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial reporting and record retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions must maintain complete lists of all expenditures; a financial report based on these lists required for the full grant period from each team member at the end of the grant. All invoices, pay-slips, etc. must be retained for at least two years after the end of the grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting practices may be modified if required by HFSPO Board or auditors. Be prepared for audits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical conduct requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Awardees must observe the highest ethical standards and conform strictly to national and institutional codes, regulations and laws governing ethical conduct of scientific research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions must inform HFSPO of infringements. Awardees must agree not to undertake research jointly where procedures forbidden in their own labs are permissible elsewhere. See HFSP Good Scientific Practice and scientific misconduct policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of private or sensitive personal data
rubrics_metrics.description: If research involves collection/processing of sensitive personal data (health, sexual lifestyle, ethnicity, political opinion, religion, genetic information, etc.) applicants must justify the need, discuss ethical implications and describe how they will address them, including informed consent and authorization for secondary use if using existing data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe whether videos/photographs will be used publicly and methods to guarantee privacy. Specify whether existing data use has been authorized by primary owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of personal data (GDPR compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: HFSPO commits to safeguarding applicants’ personal information in accordance with GDPR (EU) 2016/679 and transfers outside EU/EEA; the HFSPO Privacy Policy explains collection, storage and use of personal information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure understanding of how HFSPO handles personal data and any applicant obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual property and publication timing
rubrics_metrics.description: HFSPO will not claim intellectual or commercial property rights generated through sponsored research. Assignment of such rights and income determined by institution procedures. Submission of manuscripts for publication must not be delayed for more than 45 working days after manuscript completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge HFSP support (with grant number/DOI) in all resulting publications. HFSPO will not become involved in IP disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: DORA / assessment on content not JIF
rubrics_metrics.description: HFSP is a signatory to DORA; reviewers evaluate proposals based on content not Journal Impact Factors. Assessment considers quality and influence of candidates’ publications (including preprints).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are advised to consider the content and influence of research outputs rather than JIF; applicants should highlight content and influence of publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of AI-assisted technologies in writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Generative AI and AI-assisted technologies may be used only to improve readability and language, not to create content. Authors are requested to disclose their use of AI; HFSP reserves the right to check use with software and take outcome into consideration in evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose any AI use in the application; do not use AI to generate scientific content or ideas without disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-publication transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must enter number, author list and titles of co-publications between team members to guide the review committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent; more than three co-publications likely seen as proof of ongoing collaboration and will strongly reduce funding chances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion, diversity, equity and accessibility encouragement
rubrics_metrics.description: HFSP encourages inclusion, diversity, equity and accessibility and welcomes applicants of any gender, origin, cultural background, and age.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are encouraged to ensure diversity of backgrounds (gender, origin, and others) in team composition as it often adds to quality.
